standard_prerequisites.name: The definition of the order of vanishing of a meromorphic section at a prime divisor, by comparing the section with a local generator at the generic point of the divisor
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the function whose additivity is the content of the proof.

standard_prerequisites.name: Meromorphic sections of an invertible module form a module over the sheaf of meromorphic functions, and the product of nonzero meromorphic sections of two invertible modules is a nonzero meromorphic section of the tensor product
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used at statement lines 6834-6839 and at proof lines 6849-6851
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes the product st a legitimate meromorphic section of the tensor product and lets the local comparison be taken.

standard_prerequisites.name: Additivity of the order function on meromorphic functions at a prime divisor
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the factorisation of the quotient into the sum of the three orders.

core_obligations: Set the local picture: let Z be a prime divisor with generic point xi, choose generators of the two invertible modules at xi, and note that their product generates the tensor product at xi (proof lines 6849-6856).

Factor the quotient: the ratio of the section st to the product of the generators is the product of the ratios of the individual sections to their generators, which reduces the additivity claim to the corresponding additivity for the order of meromorphic functions (proof lines 6857-6859).
Conclude additivity of the order at every prime divisor, and hence the equality of divisors and of Weil divisor classes stated (proof lines 6860-6863).
proof_roadmap: Compare both sides at the generic point of an arbitrary prime divisor using local generators, then invoke additivity of the order of a meromorphic function (proof lines 6849-6863).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a locally Noetherian integral scheme the divisor of a product of nonzero meromorphic sections of two invertible modules is the sum of the two divisors, and hence that Weil divisor classes are additive in the tensor product (statement lines 6830-6845). The counted proof is short and complete: it fixes a prime divisor with generic point, chooses local generators of the two modules, observes that their product generates the tensor product, and factors the quotient of the product of the sections by the product of the generators into the product of the individual quotients, at which point additivity of the order function gives the claim (proof lines 6847-6863). It is H2: the computation is carried out in the counted span and the only input is additivity of the order of a meromorphic function.
